answer: The vault decay curve is applied at each close, karst records the drop, and basalt recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 8 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 101 aliases cost 347 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
